uncited: *   **Input:** A 3D volumetric dataset $V$ where each voxel $k$ has position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $\rho_k$ (or color/intensity), and optionally a surface normal $\mathbf{n}_k$.
A camera model defined by the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix.
*   **Image Buffer:** 2D array of color and opacity values $(C_x, C_y, \alpha_x, \alpha_y)$.
For each active voxel $k$, transform its position $\mathbf{p}_k$ from volume space to screen space using the MVP matrix.
Determine the area covered by the splat (footprint) on the screen.
For parallel projection, the footprint is constant for all voxels.

*   Calculate $\text{dotV} = \mathbf{V}_{\text{toEye}} \cdot \mathbf{V}_{\text{toCamera}[i]}$, where $\mathbf{V}_{\text{toEye}}$ is the unit vector from the voxel center to the eye point, and $\mathbf{V}_{\text{toCamera}[i]}$ is the unit vector from the voxel center to the camera position.
*   Calculate $\text{dotN} = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{V}_{\text{toCamera}[i]}$, where $\mathbf{n}$ is the unit normal to the surface at the voxel center.
Render the voxel as a primitive (e.g., a square or circular quad) centered at $(x_k, y_k)$ with a size corresponding to the footprint.
The primitive is rasterized into the image buffer.
Accumulate the splatted contributions into the image buffer.
*   **Point-size / Footprint Radius:** Determines the spread of the splat.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot A)$, where $N$ is the number of voxels and $A$ is the average area (in pixels) covered by a splat.
The complexity depends on the footprint size and the density of voxels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H)$ for the image buffer, plus $O(N)$ for the voxel data.

Since the claim is a compound statement and the evidence fully supports one half but only implicitly/partially addresses the other (by describing a different, less precise method), the verdict is partial.
